proposal.reason: Trial 1 used word-only features with C=0.3 and collapsed to majority-class prediction: class_recall was [1.0, 0.0] and macro_f1 was 0.463. A word+char representation with C=3.0 is a reasonable next primary-search candidate because it adds subword cues that may help distinguish spam while retaining word features and reducing regularization relative to the failed baseline.
proposal.review: No completed trial directly evaluates this candidate, so this is an exploratory selection rather than a demonstrated improvement. The prior result is evidence of majority-class collapse, not proof that word+char features will fix it.
proposal.hypothesis: Adding character n-gram features to word features and using C=3.0 will reduce majority-class collapse by giving the logistic model more discriminative subword evidence, potentially increasing spam recall and macro_f1 relative to the word-only C=0.3 baseline.
proposal.uncertainty: The direction and magnitude of change are unknown. The candidate may overfit or may still fail to recover spam recall; there is no direct primary-split evidence for this configuration, and no formal test is available to the agent.

proposal.reason: Trial 2 showed that word+char features with C=3.0 achieved the best observed PRIMARY search macro_f1 (0.9373) but had a train-search gap of about 0.0546. The available single_word_char_C0.3 candidate keeps the same representation while increasing regularization, making it a direct and informative next PRIMARY-search test of whether the strong word+char signal can be retained with less overfitting.
proposal.review: This is not a demonstrated improvement over trial 2. Trial 1 showed majority-class collapse for word-only C=0.3, but trial 2 provides evidence that word+char features can recover spam recall. The proposed C=0.3 variant has not been evaluated on the PRIMARY split, so the effect of stronger regularization is uncertain.
proposal.hypothesis: Using word+char features with C=0.3 may preserve the discriminative subword and word cues seen in trial 2 while reducing overfitting, potentially maintaining or improving macro_f1 relative to word+char C=3.0.
proposal.uncertainty: The direction and magnitude of change are unknown. Stronger regularization may reduce the train-search gap but could also underfit and lower spam recall or macro_f1. No formal test is available, and this candidate has no direct PRIMARY-split measurement.

proposal.reason: Trial 2 is the best completed PRIMARY result so far: word+char features with C=3.0 reached macro_f1 0.9373 and recovered spam recall to 0.8022. Trial 3 kept word+char features but lowered C to 0.3 and fell to macro_f1 0.7482, suggesting stronger regularization alone underfit. The MiniLM lexical candidate adds frozen sentence-encoder features to word/char lexical features, which may provide complementary semantic signal while retaining the lexical cues that worked in trial 2. This is an exploratory PRIMARY-search choice, not a demonstrated improvement.
proposal.review: No completed trial directly evaluates MiniLM lexical features, so this is not evidence-backed as an improvement. Trial 2 supports word+char lexical features at C=3.0, while trial 3 shows that word+char with C=0.3 was substantially weaker. The proposed candidate uses C=0.3 but adds MiniLM features, so the net effect is uncertain and may still underfit or overfit.
proposal.hypothesis: Adding frozen MiniLM sentence-encoder features to word/char lexical features may supply complementary semantic evidence that helps the logistic classifier distinguish spam from ham, potentially improving macro_f1 relative to lexical-only configurations. The direction and magnitude are unknown.
proposal.uncertainty: There is no direct PRIMARY-split measurement for MiniLM lexical features. The C=0.3 setting may underfit as in trial 3, and the added encoder features may not improve spam recall or macro_f1. No formal test is available to the agent, so this is exploratory.
